_comment: Read by the detect-changes job of 5_builderpackage_manager-multiples.yml (three-dot diff of the pull request, matched with github_glob_to_regex: positive globs only, `**` spans directories, there is no `!` negation) and by 5_testintegration_manager.yml on manual dispatch.
_comment_exclude: Changed files matching one of these never select a module: unit-test trees (both the `tests/` and the singular `test/` spelling), qa/ harnesses, benchmarks, mocks, developer tooling, the packaging of other products and Markdown. None is compiled into or installed by the package the suites run against (the package build passes neither TEST nor ENGINE_TEST), and the workflow's own `paths` keeps the same trees from firing it. tests/integration/** is deliberately not here.
_comment_infra: Every module repeats the plumbing that can change any suite's result: the two workflows, this file, the interpreter version, the package hand-off action, the certificate tool, and the build configuration every binary of the package goes through (src/Makefile, src/CMakeLists.txt, src/cmake/**, src/external/CMakeLists.txt, src/deps.lock.mk: flags, hardening, jemalloc, RUNPATH and the versions of the external libraries). The control script, the systemd unit and the credential resolver every job runs before its tests are manager_control's.

modules.name: api
modules._comment_tiers: Each element produces one matrix row; space-separated values become individual --tier flags
modules._comment_rbac: rbac tests live under test_api/test_rbac/ — covered as a subset of test_api/. The whole framework is listed because apid serves every request through it (DAPI, RBAC, sockets), and manager_config because test_config uploads wazuh-manager.conf.
modules._comment_paths: framework/setup.py, requirements.txt and .python-version decide what the embedded interpreter holds (src/Makefile install_dependencies, install_framework, install_api); framework/wrappers/generic_wrapper.sh launches every Python CLI. The daemons the API only reads through (wazuh-db for /agents, the engine, remoted) are not listed: their own modules and manager_control cover them.

modules.name: wazuh_db
modules._comment_tiers: wazuh-db integration tests are all tier 0 (smoke/functional against the wdb socket)
modules._comment_paths: wdb_lib links wazuh_uds_http_server for wdb-http.sock (src/wazuh_db/CMakeLists.txt:102-104) and includes shared_modules/common (:40). Every C daemon links libwazuh (src/shared/**), libconfig and, through it, manager_config (src/config/CMakeLists.txt:68-75), and loads wazuh-manager.conf with w_mconf_load()/w_mconf_section() (src/config/src/mconf-config.c); shared_modules/utils is on the include path of its C++ sources. (src/wazuh_db/CMakeLists.txt:41,102-103).

modules.name: manager_control
modules._comment: Regression coverage for wazuh-manager-control (a restarted daemon killed on a stale-pidfile PID collision, the start lock, refused starts, a restart during a reload) and the start smoke of the whole installed package.
modules._comment_paths: This is the only suite that starts, restarts and reloads all seven daemons and asserts each one is running (test_restart_during_reload, test_refused_start_keeps_running, test_pid_collision_recovery), through the systemd unit and wazuh-manager-control, on the configuration the DEB postinst generates. So it is selected by everything the .deb builds, installs and loads at start -- the closure of 5_builderpackage_manager-multiples.yml's own `paths`: the daemons and the libraries they link (src/**: the engine is wazuh-manager-analysisd, modulesd loads every module .so), the Python plane (apid, clusterd), the configuration templates and internal options (etc/**), the control script, the credential resolver its checkcredentials() runs (src/init/**), install.sh, the DEB recipe and maintainer scripts, mitre.db (opened by wazuh-db) and the downloads `make deps` resolves. Without it a change under src/engine, src/shared, src/wazuh_modules or etc built four packages and started none of them. Only the .deb is installed (5_testintegration_manager.yml dpkg -i), so the RPM spec is not listed; unit-test, qa and benchmark trees are removed by the top-level "exclude".
